This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the London City Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 22 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the London City Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/gb/london/EGLC.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Official forecasts from the Met Office and supporting models indicate a dry, high-pressure regime with northerly flow and mostly sunny conditions for London on August 22, supporting a daily maximum near the seasonal average of 21–22 °C. Light winds and limited cloud cover allow efficient daytime heating without significant advection of warmer air, keeping values tightly clustered around these levels. Trader consensus, reflected in the closely matched 44.5 % implied probability for 21 °C and 37.5 % for 22 °C, captures residual uncertainty from small variations in afternoon insolation, boundary-layer mixing, or minor model spread in peak timing. Updated guidance through the evening of August 21 will refine resolution criteria for the highest recorded temperature.

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecast consensus from multiple models shows Paris reaching a daily maximum of 23–24°C on August 22 under mostly clear to partly cloudy skies with light northerly winds. This positioning reflects modest high-pressure building after cooler, unsettled conditions on August 21, limiting daytime heating while allowing sufficient insolation for temperatures to approach the long-term August average high near 25°C. eventMetadata.context_description:
**Persistent cloud cover, showers, and high atmospheric moisture are the dominant factors capping daytime heating in Seoul/Incheon on August 22, 2026, keeping market-implied odds clustered tightly around 27–29 °C.**

Official guidance from the Korea Meteorological Administration and multiple numerical models (GFS, ECMWF analogs) indicate overcast skies with 60–95 % rain probability through much of the day, light easterly winds of 4–7 mph, and dew points near 23–25 °C. These conditions sharply reduce incoming solar radiation and promote evaporative cooling, preventing temperatures from climbing much above the mid-to-upper 20s °C. Recent developments reinforce this: heavy rain on the 21st has left saturated soils and a moist boundary layer that will take time to modify, while the steering pattern favors continued cloudiness rather than rapid clearing.

The narrow spread between the leading contracts (28 °C at 36.5 %, 29 °C at 31.0 %, 27 °C at 19.0 %) reflects genuine forecast uncertainty in the precise timing and coverage of showers versus any brief afternoon breaks in cloud. A few-tenths of a degree Celsius difference hinges on whether insolation peaks for 1–2 hours or remains suppressed all day—variables that current model runs still diverge on. Higher outcomes (30 °C+) carry low probability because sustained clearing would require a faster eastward shift of the rain shield than currently projected. Lower readings (≤26 °C) are similarly discounted given the expected modest diurnal rise once any morning precipitation eases. Traders are therefore weighting the most recent model consensus on modest warming under persistent stratus and stratocumulus.

Traders assign the highest implied probabilities to 31°C and 32°C because small differences in rainfall timing or intensity could shift the daily peak by 1–2°C. Updated IMD and global model runs expected in the next 24–48 hours will refine these ranges ahead of market resolution.

This setup limits insolation while promoting evaporative cooling and cloud shading that caps daytime peaks near historical August averages of 32–33°C. Short-range ensemble guidance clusters tightly around 33–34°C, yet modest uncertainty persists in the timing and intensity of convective cells versus clearer intervals that could allow brief warming to 35°C. Traders weight 34°C and 35°C most heavily because resolution hinges on the precise balance between regional humidity, sea-breeze influences, and any last-model-run shifts in steering flow before the 48-hour window closes.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 23 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/ph/manila/RPLL.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: The closely matched market-implied probabilities for 30°C (31.5%) and 31°C (30.5%) as Manila’s highest temperature on August 23 reflect the narrow range of official forecasts amid active southwest monsoon (habagat) conditions. PAGASA guidance for the date projects daytime maxima of 30–32°C with 60–80% rain chances and scattered thunderstorms, while longer-range models such as AccuWeather place the typical August high near 30°C (87°F). Persistent cloud cover and frequent showers limit solar heating and suppress peaks relative to clearer periods, producing the observed clustering around 30–31°C; any reduction in rainfall timing or intensity could allow brief clearing and a push toward 32°C, whereas heavier or earlier convection would favor the lower end. Historical August climatology for Manila shows average highs of 30–31°C, providing a baseline that traders are weighting against the current monsoon-enhanced moisture and instability.
